correctness.rationale: The phase integral vanishes unless spectator exponents agree and gives the stated Fourier coefficient otherwise. With the unweighted squared moduli distributed as Dirichlet(1,...,1), the moment parameter for each variable in a cross entry is 1 plus half the sum of its two exponents. Monomial normalization cancels the common Γ(d+m) denominator and the spectator factorials, leaving exactly the two-coordinate gamma quotient. Stars and bars gives the multiplicities for d≥3; d=2 has only the top-degree block. On the complex two-sphere model (unit sphere in C²), multiplying by z₁ and z₂ splits both numerator and denominator of the quotient into two terms, so the two block extrema are nested in the required directions as degree increases. Direct reduction of the quadratic matrix by interchange of its outer coordinates gives the antisymmetric level and the two symmetric roots; the off-diagonal first- and second-harmonic entries are 3 sin(theta)/(8 sqrt(2)) and sin(2 theta)/(4 pi). The gamma roots lie strictly outside delta±sin(theta)/4, and |c|<sin(theta)/4 puts the antisymmetric level strictly between them. Only its collision with delta at theta=pi/2 survives, and only when the spectator-only branch is present. At that angle the eigenvectors with normalized monomial coefficients (1,±sqrt(2),1) give (z₁±z₂)². Each nonzero restriction and its complement have positive mass by analyticity. Finally, the norms of the mth powers of z₁±z₂ on the C² sphere are 2^m/(m+1) when squared; the pointwise bounds on the unwanted side give the displayed exponential limits at each fixed interior angle. The recorded finite quadratures, symbolic cubic, and numerical spectra are corroboration, not the proof of universal spectral order.
residual_risks: The tilted Dirichlet parameters at proof line 53 refer to weighting by a squared normalized monomial, not to unweighted surface measure. Exact sharpness is claimed for the fixed-degree edge values, not for the asymptotic estimates or for apertures approaching the boundary with m.
